newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG SEEK MUCH NEEDED HOME WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG SEEK MUCH NEEDED HOME WIN.

text.p: Only last year regarded by many as the world's best goalkeeper, Bernard Lama's alarming drop in form mirrors the critical state of his team Paris St Germain.
PSG are at home to Cannes on Saturday in a match which would normally be regarded a formality, but has taken on new meaning with their desperate need for a rehabilitating victory.
The 1994 champions' season could be roughly divided into a before and after Lama's knee injury, ironically away to Cannes in mid-September.
Lama was unbeaten in nearly seven full games from the start of the season, coming off seven minutes from time at Cannes after hurting his knee saving a penalty.
He underwent cartilage surgery and, with PSG floundering and in danger of going out of the European Cup Winners' Cup, Lama came back early.

He helped them qualify for the quarter-finals with a 4-0 second leg victory over Galatasaray of Turkey at the Parc des Princes in late October after they had lost the away leg 4-2, their first defeat of the season, without him.
But that masked a truth soon to become evident -- that Lama had hurried his return from the operation.
Lama is 33 and former France keeper Bruno Martini, also injured in his 30s, said: "To be injured between 30 and 35 is not the same as at 20 or 25. You recover a lot less quickly."

PSG, who had begun to ship goals through reserve Vincent Fernandez although their only defeat was away to Galatasaray, lost a 13-match unbeaten run in the league at Rennes in late October with Lama back in goal.

They have since dropped crucial points at home to teams in the relegation zone, been beaten 5-3 at Nantes, were crushed 6-1 at home by Juventus in the European Super Cup and then, critically, lost 2-0 last Sunday to Monaco.
Lama, with PSG plunging deep into crisis, has even lost the captain's armband to midfielder Rai, confidant of fellow Brazilian, manager Ricardo.

His self doubts also pushed Lama to take seriously the team's decision not to talk to journalists in the build-up to last weekend's top-of-the-table clash at Monaco. "Do you want me to go there in a losing frame of mind?" he asked.

But seldom could Lama be blamed for a blunder, rather he just lost the superb early season form, an extension of his international performances at Euro 96, that exuded confidence and rubbed off on the defence.

That was until last weekend at Monaco where he was at fault with the first goal of the defeat that left PSG seven points adrift and looking more realistically at second place in the championship at the end of the season.
